Acervulo observed in a permanent preparation of the asexual phase of Ventura inaequalis at 10xGoogle Lens Ai overviewThe image shows a micrograph of a plant tissue infected by the fungus Venturia inaequalis, the causative agent of apple scab. 
The image highlights key structures of the pathogen within the host tissue:
Conidióforos cortos conidios: These are short conidiophores bearing conidia (asexual spores), which are the reproductive structures of the fungus found just beneath the host cuticle during the growing season. 
Plecténquima: This refers to the fungal tissue, or a type of fungal mycelial aggregation, that colonizes the host plant's tissue. 
Translation:
